verdict.rationale: AnyDesk ships its own REST API and CLI. The API covers listing and inspecting clients, retrieving session history, closing sessions, editing session comments and changing client aliases. The CLI covers install, configuration, connection and removal. However, the portal also manages address books, users, roles, permissions and custom clients, and nothing in the evidence exposes those through the API, so UI parity is clearly not demonstrated. Missing for 10: API coverage of address books, user/role/permission management and custom-client configuration; any documented statement of UI parity; a published OpenAPI spec (probe found none); independent corroboration of API breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: You can use the API to integrate AnyDesk data with third-party systems, for example, to automate billing or collect session logs.
List all AnyDesk clients registered to the account; Get details for a specific client (e.g., Alias, online status)
Retrieve Session History for a selected time range ... Close an active session
Add or update session comments ... Change a client Alias; Remove a client Alias
The AnyDesk Command-Line Interface (CLI) allows advanced users and IT administrators to automate installation, configuration, connection, and removal tasks.
